title: South Street rezoning and development charge reduction application
subtitle: Also stormwater rate study, Elora Mill phasing, road salt resolution, speed limits, water softener rebates and audited financials.
overview: Council approved a rezoning to allow 23 townhouse units at 191 Wellington Road 7 and 290 South Street in Salem {{vote:m11}}. Two delegates asked for a deferral, citing density, neighbourhood character and an alternative resident proposal. Staff said the application had been revised and that a deferral could lead to an appeal for non-decision.

Council directed staff to apply to Ontario's Development Charge Reduction Program {{vote:m18}}. Staff changed their approach after new provincial guidance arrived days earlier. Council also received a draft stormwater rate study and sent it to ConnectCW for input {{vote:m8}}, endorsed a water softener rebate program {{vote:m10}}, and adopted a road salt resolution urging provincial action {{vote:m16}}.

Other decisions included allowing a change to the Elora South development phasing under its tax increment grant agreement {{vote:m15}}, lowering speed limits on five roads {{vote:m14}}, and approving the 2025 audited financial statements {{vote:m19}}. After closed session, the Mayor reported only that direction was given to the CAO and that the matters stay confidential until agreements are executed.

decisions.item: Zoning amendment RZ07-2025, South Street, Salem
decisions.detail: Council approved rezoning of 191 Wellington Road 7 and 290 South Street from R1A to an R3 exception zone for 23 townhouse units and gave the by-law three readings.
Council directed staff to apply to the provincial program, quantify a residential development charge reduction, and delegated authority to sign related agreements if successful.
Council received the draft study for information and directed staff to post it on ConnectCW, deferring further public information sessions to the next term of Council.
Council delegated authority to the CAO and CFO to sign an amendment to the Elora South Inc. grant agreement reflecting the new development phasing.
Council received the 2026 Salt Management Plan and adopted a resolution urging the Province to create limited liability legislation and an expert advisory committee.
Council authorized a new speed by-law lowering limits on Middlebrook Rd., Noah Rd., Parkside Dr. W., Woodside St. and St. Andrew St. E.
Council endorsed a rebate program for demand-based and salt-free water softening systems, including eligible homes in chloride-affected areas of Fergus and Elora.

decisions.item: Compact pickup truck for by-law enforcement
decisions.detail: Council awarded the tender to Trillium Ford Lincoln Ltd for up to $43,695.00 before HST and approved revised funding.

debate: Two delegates opposed the South Street rezoning as out of character with the neighbourhood and nearby heritage area. They said an alternative resident proposal and related correspondence were missing from the staff report, and compared the density with the Sideroad 19 approval. They asked for deferral.

Staff and several councillors said all required information had been received and that the application had been revised, including fewer front-facing units and a two-storey height limit. Staff said a deferral could lead to an appeal for non-decision. One councillor said legal costs from planning appeals are rising and supported infill as a way to limit sprawl.

On the development charge program, staff said new provincial guidance on eligible costs and timing made the original plan, which removed several major projects from the background study, too risky. They proposed tying the application to a new well. Councillors asked about the effect on other projects, the length of the freeze and whether savings would reach home buyers. Staff said no mechanism was indicated for that.

On Elora South, councillors asked about earlier talk of affordable housing, public parking in the proposed garage and the effect on the Carlton Place reconstruction. Staff said Carlton Place stays in year 10 of the capital forecast until funding is settled and that any extra parking floor would need rezoning.

On the stormwater rate study, councillors asked about links to water use, credits for green infrastructure and whether rural properties should pay. The consultant said measured impervious area is the fairest basis. Rural ditch costs are a small share, and credits could be considered after public input.
